Solution[edit]

For every permutation of x(i) there is a sequence {y(n)}, and we call y1+2y2+…+ny(n) its S value. Noticing the importance role Zero plays here, we discuss different cases of permutations in relation to Zero.

Case 1: all permutations with S values greater than or equal to Zero. Take the permutation in descending order: a1>=a2>=…>=a(n), let S(a) denote its S value, and a(i,j)=a(i)+a(i+1)+…+a(j), i<j. We now find the upper bound of a(k,n). a(k)>=a(k+1),…,a(n) → a(k)>=a(k+1,n)/(n-k). If a1+a2+…+a(n)=-1, then since S(a) is the sum of pairing products in opposite order of {a(n)} and {n}, per Chebyshev’s Inequality, S(a)<=(a1+…+a(n))(1+…+n)/n=-(n+1)/2<0, in contradiction to all S>=0! So a1+a2+…+a(n)=1. a1,…,a(k)>=a(k) → 1=a1+…+a(n)=a1+…+a(k)+a(k+1,n)>=k•a(k)+a(k+1,n)>=k•a(k+1,n)/(n-k)+a(k+1,n)=n/(n-k)•a(k+1,n) → a(k+1,n)<=(n-k)/n, or a(k,n)<=(n-k+1)/n. Then a1+2a2+…+na(n)=a(1,n)+a(2,n)+…+a(n-1,n)+a(n,n)<=1+(n-1)/n+(n-2)/n+…+1/n=(n+1)/2 → 0<=S(a)<=(n+1)/2 → |S(a)|<=(n+1)/2.

Case 2: all permutations with S values less than or equal to Zero. Take the permutation in ascending order: b1<=b2<=…<=b(n), let S(b) denote its S value. If b1+b2+…+b(n)=1, then since S(b) is the sum of pairing products in same order of {a(n)} and {n}, per Chebyshev’s Inequality, S(b)>=(b1+…+b(n))(1+…+n)/n=(n+1)/2>0, in contradiction to all S<=0! So b1+b2+…+b(n)=-1. Ditto, b(k,n)>=-(n-k+1)/n → b1+2b2+…+nb(n)=b(1,n)+b(2,n)+…+b(n-1,n)+b(n,n)>=-1-(n-1)/n-(n-2)/n-…-1/n=-(n+1)/2 → 0>=S(b)>=-(n+1)/2 → |S(b)|<=(n+1)/2.

Case 3: all permutations with S values spanning across Zero (the hard one). Let S1<=0 be the smallest value in all permutations, and S(r)>0 be the largest, denote values of all terms of x(i) in ascending order: t1<=t2<=…<=t(n), per Rearrangement’s Inequality, t1+2t2+…+nt(n)>=t1’+2t2’+…+nt(n)’>=t(n)+2t(n-1)+…+nt1, {t(n)’} representing permutations in random order. In {x(n)} let t1=x(i), 1<=i<=n, now use the following method to transport value t1 to x1, step by step. First we switch the values of x(i) with x(i-1), and move value t1 to x(i-1), let S1 be the S value of {x(n)}, and S2 be the S value of the new sequence after the switch, now we notice that between the above two S values no terms are changed except the ones including x(i) and x(i-1). Now let M be the sum of the unchanged terms, we have S1=M+(i-1)x(i-1)+ix(i), S2=M+(i-1)x(i)+ix(i-1) → |S2-S1|=|M+(i-1)x(i)+ix(i-1)-M-(i-1)x(i-1)+ix(i)|=|x(i-1)-x(i)|, since it is given that |x(i)|<=(n+1)/2 → |x(i-1)-x(i)|<=n+1 → |S2-S1|<=n+1. This means during this move the change in S value does not exceed n+1. Repeat the above operation, each time value t1 moves backward by one term, and through finite steps arrives at x1. Same as the first step, during the migration of t1 the change in S value does not exceed n+1: |S(i+1)-S(i)|<=n+1. Now continue this to all other values: t2,…,t(n), and transport each of them to the place matching its ranking in value, i,e, t(i)=x(i), i=2~n, therefore eventually the sequence is turned into the ascending order. Same with t1, each time a t(i) completes its migration, the change in S value will never exceed n+1. Assume it takes m steps to transform the original sequence into ascending order, i.e., S(m+1)=t1+2t2+…+nt(n), then a new sequence is generated: S1,S2,…,S(m+1), also|S(i+1)-S(i)|<=n+1, i=1~m. Given that S1<=0, and per Rearrangement’s Inequality S(m+1)>=S(r)>0, so S1 and S(m+1) bear different signs, then Zero must be between S1 and S(m+1), in other words between two consecutive terms, let them be S(p) and S(p+1). We now know that the difference between any two consecutive terms of {S(m+1)} is less than or equal to n+1, therefore |S(p+1)-S(p)|<=n+1, so one of them must be at the distance of less than or equal to (n+1)/2 to Zero, WLOG, let that be S(p), then it follows that |S(p)|<=(n+1)/2.

Summing it all up, we have that under all circumstances there always exists a permutation {y(n)} of {x(n)} such that |y1+2y2+…+ny(n)|<=(n+1)/2. Done.

This solution which centered on the special number Zero was inspired by the Sunday Mass and Pope’s Angelus Prayer at Vatican City on the date of October 4th 2026.

——TX 2026.10.6
